LAYOUT: one-page portrait PDF, warm cream (#F4ECD8) background, a short founder note set in a single warm-serif column, a small colour-swatch reference box at the foot. Converts cleanly (real page layout).

TITLE: How Fennhollow should feel

BODY:
Sun lit. Warm. Natural. A little restrained. Made by real people, in the valley.
Not a wellness tonic and not a supermarket soda -- somewhere honest in between.

Our green is the label green. The true chip lives on the printed swatch card in the studio (the Pantone chip taped inside the folder) -- use THAT, not a guess off a screen.

Type should be warm and human and easy to read over a photograph. Never shout.

Everything should look like one summer afternoon.

FOOT SWATCH BOX: a single green chip labelled 'LABEL GREEN -- see swatch card' (no hex, no Pantone number printed here).

assets.defect_engineered: the printed card reads as five tidy stacked fields (can image, NOW POURING label, flavour name, store + town, price flag), but the NOW POURING label, the flavour name, the store name and the town are ONE continuous text story in one frame so field offsets must be reconstructed from the story text; the amber price flag is a DECORATIVE grouped vector path (the price number lives in its own small story over it, not in the flag); there IS one real can picture frame at the top (unlike a decorative roundel), which is where the per-row can binds; the media box equals the trim with NO bleed box, so a can image built to run to the top edge cannot be delivered press-ready with bleed
assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the card printer's existing summer shelf-talker press PDF (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered downstream into a live data-merge template).

Document: single shelf-talker, 90 x 130 mm PORTRAIT, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded. This is the card the printer already runs a proof of and clips on the grocer's shelf rail under the cans.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (five apparent stacked fields):
- Top: a CAN IMAGE sitting on the warm cream ground, filling the top of the card to the trim edge.
- Under it: a small NOW POURING label in the humanist sans, letterspaced, on a thin rhubarb-rose rule.
- Under that: the FEATURED FLAVOUR name in the friendly display cut, large (e.g. Elderflower & Lime).
- Under that: the STORE NAME in the display cut, medium, with the TOWN under it in the sans, small.
- Lower right: a PRICE FLAG, a small rounded amber tag device with the price number reversed out of it.
- Foot: the botanical sourcing line and the co-packer nutrition claim in small sans, fixed on every card.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- There IS a real rectangular graphic/picture frame at the top for the can, so a per-row can binds into it -- this is the only picture frame on the card, and it is what makes the image merge possible.
- BUT the NOW POURING label, the FEATURED FLAVOUR name, the STORE NAME and the TOWN are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame flowing top to bottom, not four addressable frames, so every field offset has to be computed from the reconstructed story string rather than read off the mapping tool.
- The PRICE FLAG is a DECORATIVE grouped vector device (a rounded amber tag path), NOT a field and NOT a picture frame; the price NUMBER is set in its own separate short story sitting over the flag, so a price mapped into the flag lands nowhere and the price must be resolved to that small story.
- The sourcing line and the nutrition claim are static content baked into the template, not fields, and the claim cannot be reworded.
- So the frame inventory a conversion exposes (roughly: one top picture frame + one long flowing text story + one small price story + one decorative tag path group + the fixed foot text) is nothing like the five tidy stacked fields the printed card suggests.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, and the can image is designed to run to the top trim edge, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from this file however the render is called; a full-bleed can will show a hairline white sliver at the trim. The shortfall has to be reported rather than claimed away.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): STORE_NAME | TOWN | FEATURED_FLAVOUR | SHELF_PRICE | CAN_IMAGE

Colours: Warm Cream Ground #F4ECD8 card ground, Label Green #3F6B3A flavour name, Deep Ink #2C2A24 store name and body, Afternoon Amber #E5AF54 price flag, Rhubarb Rose #C56E68 the NOW POURING rule.
